Storm, fire and damage

Emergency asbestos clean up, after storm, fire or impact

Clean up of asbestos exposed or broken up by storm, fire or accidental damage. The material is the same; what is different is that nobody chose for it to be disturbed, the area is usually not secure, and the first priority is stopping it spreading further. Call with the address and what has happened, and we will organise the licensed clean up.

0456 220 552

Removal by licensed asbestos removalists. Max holds demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Stop and secure the area

    Who You, immediately

    Keep people out. Do not sweep, hose, vacuum or handle the material. Each of those spreads it.

  2. 02

    Assess what has been disturbed

    Who Max, with the licensed removalist

    How far it has gone and whether it reached soil, which changes the scope considerably.

  3. 03

    Engage the licensed removalist

    Who Max

    Damaged bonded material may have to be treated as friable, which changes the licence class.

  4. 04

    Notify where required

    Who Max and you

    Notification requirements depend on the material and the circumstances. Your insurer will usually want to be told early too.

  5. 05

    Independent assessor engaged

    Who Max

    Air monitoring and clearance, by somebody independent of the removalist.

  6. 06

    Record what happened

    Who You

    Photographs before anything is touched, and the dates. Insurers and assessors both ask.

The detail

What to do, and what not to do

  • Do not sweep it. Sweeping broken fibro is the single most effective way to put fibres into the air and spread them across a wider area.
  • Do not hose it. Washing material into drains and soil turns a contained problem into a contaminated ground problem.
  • Do not vacuum it. An ordinary vacuum passes fibres straight through and distributes them.
  • Do not handle or bag it yourself. Even with the best intentions, unwrapped material in a household bin is both unlawful and a risk to whoever handles it next.
  • Do keep people and pets away. Barriers and distance, until somebody licensed has assessed it.
  • Do photograph it first. Before anything is touched. Your insurer and the assessor will both want to see the original state.

If it reached the soil, the scope changes

Material broken up on the ground becomes a soil contamination question, which is classified and priced differently from a surface clean up.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

A storm has broken my fibro roof. What do I do first?
Keep everyone away from the area, do not sweep or hose anything, and photograph it from a distance. Then call somebody licensed. The instinct to tidy it up is the one that makes it worse.
Is damaged bonded material still bonded?
Often not, in practical terms. Material that has been broken, burnt or weathered badly enough may have to be handled as friable, which is a higher licence class with heavier controls.
Will my insurer cover it?
That is between you and your insurer, and we have no part in it. What helps is photographs taken before anything was touched, and keeping the clearance certificate and disposal dockets.
How fast can you be there?
We will tell you honestly when we can attend rather than promise a response window. What matters more in the first hour is that nobody disturbs the material further.
After a fire, is the asbestos still a problem?
Fire damaged asbestos material is usually more friable than it was, not less, and fire debris can carry it well beyond the building. It should be assessed before anyone enters to clean up.
